items.caption:
Swipe to see the startup two IIT-Delhi grads quit high-paying jobs to build.

ByteAsk makes an AI coding agent for C and C++, the languages behind trading systems, robots, cars and chips. The agent writes code and then verifies its own work, and the company is aiming at enterprise teams in defense, aerospace, robotics, automotive and semiconductors.

Founders Anirudha Kulkarni and Pratyush Saini reportedly gave up over ₹1.3 crore in combined salaries. ByteAsk has now raised $1 million in pre-seed funding from Y Combinator, where it is part of the Fall 2026 batch, and Entrepreneur First, along with angel investors.

Kulkarni previously built low-latency C++ systems at Optiver, and Saini worked on AI infrastructure at ThirdAI. This is their second company after legal-tech startup LawSutra AI, and the team is now being built across San Francisco and Bengaluru.

Sources: Hindustan Times, American Bazaar, Analytics India Magazine.

items.caption:
Swipe to see the startup putting an AI sales rep inside American factories.

Forgepoint builds Frank, an AI assistant that prepares and sends price quotes for manufacturers, plugging into the systems they already use. Factories pay for it so their estimators and sales teams can answer more requests for quotes, faster.

The New York company raised a $9.8 million seed round led by Primary Venture Partners and a16z speedrun, with angel investors from OpenAI, Brex, Vercel and SoFi.

The problem is simple: many manufacturers can make a part faster than they can send back a price. Forgepoint says it reached seven-figure annual recurring revenue within six months of launching Frank, and that customers have cut time-to-quote by more than 55% while quoting about 30% more work each month.

Sources: Tech Funding News, American Bazaar.

items.caption:
Swipe to see the startup building a therapy home for the LGBTQ+ community.

Allswell offers online therapy, group programs and trauma-informed care for LGBTQ+ adults. It makes money by billing commercial insurance and Medicaid, so patients are not stuck paying out of pocket.

The Techstars company raised a $7 million seed round led by Rethink Impact, with Magnify Ventures, Ulu Ventures and Hopelab Ventures joining existing investors Techstars and Amboy Street Ventures. Total funding is now $8.3 million including its $1.3 million pre-seed.

Co-founder Dawn Androphy has said the idea was once dismissed as too small a market. Since launching in spring 2025, Allswell says it has reached more than 1,500 billable sessions a month in DC, Maryland and Virginia, and it plans to add medication management next year.

Sources: Techstars, Behavioral Health Business.

items.caption:
Swipe to see the startup bringing AI agents to the business of selling industrial materials.

Emanate sells an AI engine to industrial distributors that handles quoting, pricing, prospecting and account management, work their sales teams have long done by hand.

Koch Disruptive Technologies, the venture arm of Koch, is making a strategic investment in the San Francisco startup. The amount was not disclosed. Emanate came out of stealth in February with backing from a16z's American Dynamism fund, Peter Thiel and Reddit co-founder Alexis Ohanian.

Founder Kiara Nirghin is a Thiel Fellow and Stanford AI researcher, and the company has fewer than 10 people. Its agents begin with a human in the loop and earn the right to act on their own as they prove results. Koch, which reports more than $125 billion in yearly revenue, says the tie-up extends to some of its own companies.

Sources: Fortune, Fast Company.

items.caption:
Swipe to see how much the defense startup Anduril is worth now.

Anduril builds drones, autonomous systems and the software that ties them together, and sells them mainly to the US military and its allies.

Congrats @anduril

The company is running an employee tender offer that would value it at about $90 billion. Current and former employees can sell shares at $94.80 each, with the offer capped at roughly $1.3 billion. It opened October 13 and closes November 9.

That is a big jump from May, when a $5 billion round led by Thrive Capital and a16z doubled Anduril's valuation to $61 billion. This is also the first tender open to staff in 16 countries, after earlier ones were limited to the US, UK and Australia. Tenders like this let early employees turn paper wealth into cash without the company going public.

Sources: CNBC, Bloomberg.
